newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: French strike creates Dutch logjam - KLM.
newsitem.headline: French strike creates Dutch logjam - KLM.

text.p: KLM Cargo, the air cargo wing of KLM Royal Dutch Airlines, is facing a bottleneck of trucked airfreight at Schiphol airport because of the French truck drivers' strike, spokesman Peter Wellhuener told Reuters.
The strike has prevented trucks carrying airfreight from making the journey from the Netherlands through France to its air cargo hub in Zaragoza, southern Spain, he stated.

The problem is an expensive one, costing the Dutch airline "hundreds of thousands of guilders," he said adding that KLM Cargo has been forced to charter in ad hoc aircraft capacity to relieve what he described as a serious bottleneck of air cargo at Schiphol which would normally have been trucked to Spain.

Wellheuner would not give specific figures about the amount of freight which has been trapped at the leading Dutch airport. Nor would he say how much extra aircraft capacity the airline has chartered in, but he added that the longer the strike continues, the bigger a problem it becomes for the airline and its shipper customers.

KLM Cargo operates a number of similar hubs for trucked airfreight throughout Europe, although its Zaragoza facility is one of the most significant in the airline's hub and spoke freight distribution system. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
